      DAY Thursday training 50m "Upper Pull Deload":

          cable_row 2x10..12 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          face_pull 2x12..15 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
          bicep_curl 2x10..12 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:

          back_stretch 60s
          shoulder_stretch 60s
      DAY Friday training 50m "Full Lower Deload":
        warmup:
          cycling 5m
        main straight_sets:
          deadlift 2x4..5 rpe 6 rest 150 seconds
          split_squat 2x8 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          hip_thrust 2x8..10 rpe 6 rest 90 seconds
          leg_extension 2x12..15 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
          seated_calf_raise 2x12..15 rpe 6 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          pigeon_pose 60s
          hip_flexor_stretch 60s
          child_pose 60s

I don't have his actual log. All I know is what you told me: about 18 working sets per session at RPE 8.5 on compounds. I don't have his per-exercise sets, reps, loads, or how many days a week he trained.

I also have to correct my first response. You said "same exercises," but I never had his exercise list, so I picked a standard 4-day upper/lower split myself. Please check it against what he actually ran.

Here is what I prescribed against the 18-set figure:

| Session | Deload sets | vs. 18 sets |
|---|---|---|
| Monday Upper Push | 11 | -39% |
| Tuesday Lower | 11 | -39% |
| Thursday Upper Pull | 11 | -39% |
| Friday Full Lower | 10 | -44% |

Intensity drops from RPE 8.5 to RPE 6.

A typical deload cuts volume by 40-60%, or about 7-11 sets from an 18-set baseline. Mine sit at the conservative end of that range. If you want a deeper cut, I can trim to 8-9 sets per session.

If you send his real exercises, sets, reps, and loads from last week, I'll rebuild the deload from those numbers, with each lift's sets set to a fixed percentage of its previous volume.
